page.layout: One printed page. At the head, the running title "PARS SECVNDA." with page number 87 at the right. Below it, two engraved medallion portraits side by side. Under them, one column of running text. At the foot, the signature "Fff 4", set right of centre. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: FL. CL. IVLIANVS natus Constantinopoli, patre
Constantio, Constatini Magni fratre, matre Basilina, forma li-
berali fuit, ingenio callido, ad literas & ad arma apto. Huc Con-
stantius patruelis, Magni filius Constantini, adoptauit, Cæsarē
fecit, ad Gallias tuedas misit. hostes hinc profligat, Gallias Ale-
mannorum incursu vastatas, sub primum accessum, præter omnium
spem asserit, regemq; Germanorum capit. Agrippinam (quę nunc
Colonia dicitur) recipit. Deinde assensu totius exercitus Pari-
siis Imperator & Augustus vocatur an. mun. 4325. à Christo nato
3 6 3. Ad Constantium literas mittit exorans vt qui licet repu-
gnans, Imperator fit à militibus appellatus, in cōsortiū Imperij
admittatur: renuit Constatius. Ad bellum ciuile parat se Iulia-
nus, item & Constatius, qui nihilominus febre correptus, cum
deficeret successore statuit Iulianum. Adepto itaq; Imperio so-
lus rerum summa potitus Iulianus, Persis bellū mouet: verùm à
transfuga quodā Persa in insidias deductus, cùm eum hinc in-
de Parthi vrgeret, ab vno ex hostibus, & quidē fugiente, conto
percutitur: & cū Philosophis de immortalitate animæ tractās,
paulò post moritur, anno ætatis 31. Imperij, mensibus 19. à mor-
te Constantini patruelis. Hic aduersus fidem Christianam li-
bros edidit. Egna. lib. 1. Pomp. Læ. Aure. Vict.
IVVIANVS, seu Iouianus, è Pannonia, mortuo Iuliano
electus est princeps, & statim Antesignani Iuuianum clamaue-
runt: tunc qui in medio, quíque postremi erant milites, opinati
Iulianum reuixisse, ingenti lætitia effusi, choreas ducebāt. Hic
cum Parsis fœdus icit, Trāstigritanas provincias quinq; reddi-
dit: atq; Arsaci Armeniæ regi, Ro. socio, & amico, opē ferre ve-
titus est. At è Persīde rediēs hyeme aspera, ingressus cubiculum
noui tectorij, positis etiam ibi prunis, ex cruditate insuper sto-
machi periit, anno ætatis 33. Imperij mensibus 7. Vide vt supia,

page.notes: Two engraved medallion portraits above the text, not transcribed as text. Left medallion: a bearded man in profile, helmeted, with a legend reading "IVLIANVS P F AVG" (the legend is partly worn, with "D N" at the lower left). Right medallion: a younger man in profile, with a legend reading "IOVINIANVS P F AVG" (with "D N" at the lower left). Legends are set around the medallion rims and read clockwise. The line "3 6 3." is printed with spaces between the digits, copied as printed. The final word "supia," is printed with a comma and is copied as printed; it may be a printing error for "supra," but this is left as printed.
